description: SASRec predicts the next item using causal self-attention over interaction histories. Learned item and position embeddings pass through attention and feed-forward blocks; the resulting representation scores candidate items by dot product. Attention can emphasize recent actions or longer dependencies. Source: [Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/html/1808.09781v1).
motivation: Balance the simplicity useful for sparse histories with the capacity to capture longer sequential patterns. Despite the supplied title, SASRec is not a dedicated cold-start solution: unseen items lack learned interaction embeddings, and users without histories provide no personalized sequence context.
implementation_notes: Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset and retain all four dataset routes. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; save artifacts under the trial directory. Select using the pinned macro validation HR@10 only. Synchronize architecture changes with the predictor writer. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), its metrics and metric_definitions, and the SASRec compatibility interface. Use only available histories and public metadata; no review or simulator-trait assumptions. No benchmark improvement has been demonstrated.
pseudocode:
For each category:
  Load the unchanged benchmark splits.
  Form padded history sequences and shifted next-item targets.
  Encode item and position embeddings with causal attention blocks.
  Optimize sampled positive/negative binary cross-entropy at valid positions.
  Save model parameters and architecture configuration.
Evaluate through the pinned host validation procedure.
Select by macro validation HR@10 across all four categories.
Write a matching predictor with category routing.

originality.positive: The original paper introduced an influential self-attention approach to sequential recommendation.
originality.negative: The supplied idea reproduces the existing SASRec baseline and specifies no new cold-start mechanism.

future_potential.positive: Available titles and descriptions could support a separately tested content-based extension for sparse items.
future_potential.negative: Such an extension is only a hypothesis; validation gains and budget feasibility remain unmeasured.

code_difficulty.positive: Starting from the existing per-dataset baseline limits implementation work.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require consistent checkpoint loading, predictor generation, and diagnostic adapters. Score uses 10 for greatest difficulty.
